paper_title: First Constraints on Nuclear Coupling of Axionlike Particles from the Binary Neutron Star Gravitational Wave Event GW170817
coupling_convention: GeV/f_a, i.e. inverse axion decay constant in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis (Log10[GeV/f_a]); x values are m_a in eV as plotted (Log10[m_a/eV])
notes: First constraint on nuclear-coupled axionlike particles from binary neutron star inspiral GW170817. The exclusion is on the f_a-m_a plane: for axion masses m_a < 1e-11 eV, decay constants 1.6e16 GeV < f_a < 1e18 GeV are excluded at 3-sigma confidence (actual CL ~99.7%, higher than the 0.95 recorded here; schema limits to 0.90/0.95). The upper edge f_a = 1e18 GeV exists because heavier decay constants prevent the finite-density phase transition inside NSs, so the bound is a band, not a one-sided limit; only the lower boundary (1.6e16 GeV) is encoded as the flat exclusion line spanning the massless-limit extrapolation (figure extends to ~1e-20 eV) up to 1e-11 eV. Constraint is independent of axions being dark matter, so no local DM density is assumed.
